name: Ljubljana Castle
label: Ljubljana Castle
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Gallusovo nabrežje' (1 web pages); placed at the stretch of Gallusovo nabrežje nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/5821190: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Ljubljana Castle' (146 m across).
notes: Medieval hilltop castle with views over the old town.

text.description:
Ljubljana Castle sits on Castle Hill above the Old Town and is one of the city's key landmarks. It is also the easiest shot to get wrong: from close up, the hill and walls are too big to fit in a phone frame. The best answer is to step back and use the town as part of the picture. From the Gallusovo nabrežje side of the river, the row of riverside Old Town facades fills the foreground and the castle rises on its hill behind them. That gives you depth and a clear sense of place in one frame.

The castle has a long history. It was probably built in the 11th century as a medieval fortress and rebuilt in the 12th. It took on its present outline in a near-complete overhaul in the 15th century, and most of the buildings that stand today date from the 16th and 17th centuries. In the 19th century it was used as a prison, and today it is a major cultural venue. A funicular has run up the hill since 2006, so you can also photograph the town from the top.

For the classic frame, stand across the river so the castle sits above the rooftops. Keep the facades along the bottom edge and let the hill fill the upper part. If you want a wider skyline, Tivoli Park is a good alternative. Take a moment to check for people and bicycles on the riverside before you shoot.
text.geographic_location: The castle stands on Castle Hill above the Old Town, the historic centre of Ljubljana. The best photo spot is on Gallusovo nabrežje, on the opposite bank of the Ljubljanica from the castle side, looking across the river at the riverside Old Town facades.
text.directions_text: Start from the Old Town and head for the Ljubljanica riverbank. The castle lies to the east of it, up on its hill. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to get the riverside facades and the castle hill in one frame. Switch to 2x or 3x if your phone has telephoto, to bring the castle closer and keep the hill from looking small. Use ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of foreground, because it shrinks the castle.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Gallusovo nabrežje (opposite bank of the Ljubljanica from the castle side). The row of riverside Old Town facades in the foreground, with the castle rising on the hill behind them. From there you look east across the water.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines. Put the facades on the lower third and the castle on the upper third, with the hill fully visible. Keep the phone level so the buildings do not lean. If you want a wider skyline with the castle on top of its hill, Tivoli Park is an alternative viewpoint.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the castle to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky does not wash out and the walls keep their detail. Take a couple of shots in case someone walks through the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: This is a general lighting suggestion: because you are looking east, afternoon light may be behind you and fall on the facades and the castle, while morning light may come from behind the castle and make it look darker. Check the light on the day.

text.access_note: Gallusovo nabrežje is a public street with no charge to stand there; for the castle itself, check the official site before you go.

name: Tivoli Park
label: Tivoli Park
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Jakopičevo sprehajališče' (4 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Jakopičevo sprehajališče' (relation/15342459): middle (250 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/14958542: large area 'Park Tivoli' (1190 m across): previous pin kept, it lies inside.
notes: Largest city park with tree-lined promenades.

text.description:
Tivoli is the largest park in Ljubljana, and the best way to photograph it is along its central walk, Jakopičevo sprehajališče. This wide, tree-lined promenade runs straight towards the cream-coloured Tivoli Mansion, with Plečnik's lampposts on either side leading the eye along it. That makes an easy, tidy composition for a phone: a strong central line, trees framing both sides, and a clear destination at the far end.

The park was laid out in 1813 to plans by the engineer Jean Blanchard, and the architect Jože Plečnik designed the promenade when he renovated the park in the 1920s. The mansion dates from the 17th century and was given its neoclassical look in the middle of the 19th century. Photo panels are often displayed along the path, which adds interest, though they can block your view, so look at what is on show before choosing your angle.

For a calmer second picture, walk to the fish pond and the old boathouse café, Čolnarna. Trees ring the water, and it makes a quieter scene than the long avenue. If you want an overview of the park's treetops and paths with the city beyond, Mostec gives a high view, but it involves some uphill walking, so confirm the climb before going.

Allow time to wander.
text.geographic_location: Tivoli Park lies on the western side of Ljubljana's Center District, with the Šiška, Vič and Rožnik districts around it. The promenade runs from the edge of the park towards Tivoli Mansion.
text.directions_text: Start from Prešeren Square in the city centre and follow Čop and Cankar Streets towards the park, which lie on the promenade's long straight axis. On foot, allow time for the walk across the centre to the park entrance. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the straight view down the promenade. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more of the tree canopy, or to the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to bring the mansion closer and make the lampposts look more tightly packed.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Jakopičevo sprehajališče (entrance end, looking east toward Tivoli Mansion). The wide, tree-lined central promenade with Plečnik's lampposts running straight toward the neoclassical Tivoli Mansion, often with photo panels along the path.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Centre yourself on the middle of the path and turn on gridlines so the lampposts and trees stay level and balanced on both sides. Keep the mansion near the vertical centre line. If photo panels are standing along the walk, include one as foreground or step slightly to one side to avoid it. For a different view, try the pond by Čolnarna for reflections and trees, or Mostec for a high view over the canopy.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the mansion to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky looks washed out. Hold the phone at chest height with both hands for a steadier shot. Take a Live Photo if people are walking along the path, then pick the frame where the path is clearest.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: At the pond, guides recommend sunrise as a good time.

text.access_note: The promenade is a public park path that is free and open at all hours, but check the official site before you go if you want to visit the mansion or other buildings in the park.

name: Triple Bridge
label: Triple Bridge
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Prešernov trg' (4 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Prešernov trg' (relation/9375924): middle (117 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/6583849: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Triple Bridge' (54 m across).
notes: Three adjoining bridges across the Ljubljanica by Jože Plečnik.

text.description:
The Triple Bridge is three bridges side by side across the Ljubljanica River. Together they link Prešeren Square with the medieval Old Town on the opposite bank. A wooden bridge is mentioned here from 1280, and this is the oldest bridge in Ljubljana. The central stone bridge dates from 1842. In the early 1930s the architect Jože Plečnik added a footbridge on each side, set at a slight angle, so the crossing fans out like a gentle funnel. The concrete balustrades have 642 balusters, and the walkway is paved with granite blocks. The bridge has been part of UNESCO World Heritage since 2021.

It photographs well because the three spans give you strong repeating lines, and the pink Franciscan church and the market colonnade sit neatly in the same frame. The classic view is from Prešeren Square, near the Prešeren statue, looking towards the bridge. It can be hard to fit all three spans into one frame from close by, so keep the phone level, step back a little and let the church and railings fill the sides. If you want every span in one shot, walk a short way to Mesarski most (Butchers' Bridge) and shoot from there, with the river and railings in front of you.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Ljubljana, where Prešeren Square on the north-western bank meets the Old Town on the south-eastern bank of the Ljubljanica. The Franciscan church stands just beside the square.
text.directions_text: The bridge lies inside the pedestrian-only zone, so you will need to walk the last stretch. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the bridge and church. If you cannot fit all three spans, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x). Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for close shots of the balustrade and the lamps.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Prešernov trg (near the Prešeren statue, looking east toward the bridge). The three spans fanning out over the Ljubljanica, with the pink Franciscan church and the market colonnade in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and keep the horizon level so the railings do not lean. Place the central span a little off-centre and let the church fill one side. For all three spans in one frame, Mesarski most is a good alternative, with the river and the love-locked railings in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bridge to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a touch so the sky does not wash out. Try a Live Photo, as passers-by crossing the bridge can add life to the scene.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, before the crowds arrive, when the square is nearly empty. Midday and December are busy.

text.access_note: The bridge is an open public space in a pedestrian-only zone and is free to visit at all hours.
claims_not_in_sources: The ultra-wide lens (0.5x) helps to fit more of the three spans into one frame when you stand close.
Dragging the exposure slider down helps keep the sky from washing out.
A Live Photo can capture people crossing the bridge.

name: Dragon Bridge
label: Dragon Bridge
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Mesarski most' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Mesarski most' (way/867534136): middle (42 m across); moved 15 m off water.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/867533647: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Dragon Bridge' (46 m across).
notes: Art Nouveau bridge guarded by four dragon statues.

text.description: The Dragon Bridge carries traffic over the Ljubljanica River, just north of the Central Market, and it is one of the city's best-known sights. Four large copper dragons crouch on pedestals at its corners, with sixteen smaller ones along the bridge. Together with the pale concrete arch and decorated railings, they make a strong, easy-to-read subject for a phone. Construction began in 1900 and the bridge opened in 1901, with final works completed by 1907. It was built in the Vienna Secession style. It was one of Europe's earliest reinforced concrete bridges and the first of its kind in Ljubljana. It is a triple-hinged arch bridge with a span of about 33 metres, and it is now protected as a technical monument. It was first named after Emperor Franz Josef I and was renamed Dragon Bridge in 1919. Local legend says the dragons wag their tails when a virgin crosses. From there you see the whole bridge with all four dragons, and the market stalls and arcades sit in the foreground. For a different view, try a close wide shot of one dragon from the bridge itself, keeping to the pavement. You can also take a tighter zoomed shot from Resljeva cesta, with a dragon, the cathedral towers and a lamp post lined up together. Take care near the road, as the bridge is built mainly for motor traffic.
text.geographic_location: The bridge is in central Ljubljana, crossing the Ljubljanica River just north of the Central Market at Vodnik Square. It links Kopitarjeva ulica with Resljeva cesta.
text.directions_text: No tram or railway stops are listed for this spot, so start from the Central Market at Vodnik Square, which is next to the bridge. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to get the whole bridge and all four dragons in one frame. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you move right up to a dragon. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) from Resljeva cesta for a squeezed-together shot of a dragon, the cathedral towers and the lamp post.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Mesarski most (upstream (south) side, looking north). All four dragons on Zmajski most with the market stalls and arcades in the foreground, and sometimes the sun rising behind the bridge.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place the bridge's arch across the lower third, with the dragons on the pedestals near the top of the frame. Keep the phone level so the railings don't lean. Include some market arcade or river in the foreground for depth. For a change, take a close shot of one copper dragon with the city behind it, or a tight zoomed shot from Resljeva cesta. Stay on the pavement and out of the roadway.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bridge to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky is bright behind it, so the dragons keep their detail. Take a few frames, as passing people and vehicles will change each shot.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunrise and early morning are suggested for the view from Mesarski most, when the sun can rise behind the bridge. One guide suggests the west bank for afternoon and dusk light instead, so check where the sun will be at your visit time.

text.access_note: The bridge is a public road bridge that you can see and photograph from the street and nearby bridges; if you plan anything beyond a normal visit, check the official site before you go.

name: Prešeren Square
label: Prešeren Square
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Tromostovje' (4 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Tromostovje' (relation/6583849): middle (54 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/9375924: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Prešernov trg' (118 m across).
notes: Central square with the Prešeren Monument and the pink Franciscan church.

text.description: Prešeren Square is the central meeting place of Ljubljana's old town, and the view back towards it from the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje) is the classic postcard shot. From the bridge you see the bronze statue of the poet France Prešeren in the middle distance, with the pink Franciscan Church of the Annunciation filling the background. The church is baroque and dates from the 17th century. The statue, which shows the poet with a muse, was put up in 1905. Ivan Zajec designed the sculpture and Max Fabiani designed its pedestal. The square took its present round shape in 1987-88 to plans by Edvard Ravnikar, and it has been closed to ordinary motor traffic since 2007. That means you can stand and compose a photo without worrying about cars. The square and the monument were declared a cultural monument of national significance in 1991. For your phone, the bridge gives you a bit of distance, so you can use the zoom lens to bring the church facade close behind the statue. If you want a different feel, walk onto the square for a close view of the church front with the paving and people in the foreground. Or stand at the statue itself and shoot the poet with the church rising behind him. Around the festive season, a Christmas tree and event stages can block the view, so have a look before settling on a spot.
text.geographic_location: Prešeren Square is in the heart of Ljubljana's old town, at the northern end of the Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica river. The Franciscan Church stands between Čop Street and Miklosich Street, on the square's north-west to north side.
text.directions_text: There are no stops listed for this spot, so make your way to the old town on foot, as the square is in a pedestrian zone. From the Ljubljana railway station, Miklosich Street (Miklošičeva cesta) leads south to the square. From there the middle of the square is about 1 minute on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the telephoto lens (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to compress the church behind the statue. The default lens (1x) gives a wider scene with more of the square. The ultra-wide (0.5x) is best saved for the square itself, when you want everything in one frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Tromostovje (stand on the bridge and face back toward the square). The statue of France Prešeren in the middle distance with the pink Franciscan Church filling the background.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and place the statue on one of the vertical lines, with the church facade behind it. Zoom in a little so the facade looks close to the statue. If the bridge is crowded, wait a moment for a gap. For another angle, shoot the church front from the square, or the statue from close up with the church behind.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the statue to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the pink facade and the sky keep their colour. Hold the phone steady against the bridge parapet or with both elbows tucked in.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Golden hour, around sunset, is the time several guides recommend for this view.

text.access_note: This is an open public square and the statue can be visited at all hours, but check the official site before you go if festivals or events are planned.
claims_not_in_sources: The Triple Bridge may be busy with passers-by, so you may need to wait briefly for a clear view.
Zooming in with a 2x-5x phone lens makes a distant building look closer to the subject in front of it.
Lowering the exposure slightly helps keep the colour of a bright pink facade and sky.

name: Ljubljana railway station
label: Railway Station
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Trg Osvobodilne fronte' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Trg Osvobodilne fronte' (way/1553016313): middle (89 m across).
pin_note: Position from the Wikipedia article 'Ljubljana railway station'.

text.description: Ljubljana's main railway station is more of a street-level, everyday scene than a pretty postcard, but it makes a good photo for showing how people arrive in the city. The best view is from the square in front, Trg Osvobodilne fronte. From there you can frame the station's front facade and main entrance, with the bronze equestrian monument to General Maister in the park alongside as a strong foreground. The station was completed on 18 April 1848, a year before the Vienna–Trieste Southern Railway reached Ljubljana. It was renovated in 1980 by the architect Marko Mušič. A small monument to James Joyce, by the sculptor Jakov Brdar, was put up in 2003. Joyce spent a night here in 1904 after wrongly thinking he had reached Trieste. Rebuilding work began in autumn 2024, with completion planned for 2026. The facade and entrance may therefore be partly hidden by hoardings or fencing. If so, shoot the monument and the square with the building behind it, and take close shots of details instead. A second option is a platform shot of trains heading towards the Alps and the coast, but only if you are travelling and the platforms are open to you. Stay well back from the platform edge and keep off the tracks. Whichever you choose, keep pedestrians and passing traffic in the frame for a sense of scale.
text.geographic_location: In the city centre of Ljubljana. The square in front of the station, with a small park containing the General Maister monument alongside, lies to the east.
text.directions_text: No tram or railway stops are listed for this spot. From the town centre, near Ljubljana Castle and the Triple Bridge, you can walk to the station, or go by taxi. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) if the square is busy or you are close to the facade. Use the default lens (1x) for a natural view, and the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for the monument or details of the entrance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Trg Osvobodilne fronte (in front of the station facade, with the General Maister Monument park alongside). The station's front facade and main entrance, framed from the square, with the bronze equestrian monument in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the bronze horse and rider low in the frame as a foreground and let the facade fill the background. Turn on gridlines to keep the building's vertical lines straight. If works block the entrance, crop in on the monument or the Joyce monument instead. For a different view, a platform shot can show trains heading towards the Alps and the coast, but stay behind the platform edge and off the tracks.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the facade to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright so the building does not go dark. Keep the phone level to avoid leaning walls.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Daylight, ideally when the square is quieter and the light is soft. Early morning may be calmer, though that depends on the day and on the works.

text.access_note: The square is an open public space, but the station is a working building under reconstruction, so check the official site before you go and stay off tracks and railway land.

name: Ljubljana Castle funicular
label: Castle Funicular
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Krekov trg' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Krekov trg' (way/1036984484): middle (95 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/144464067: the middle of the OpenStreetMap line 'Ljubljana Castle funicular' (3 m long).
notes: Glass funicular up to the castle.

text.description: The Ljubljana Castle funicular is a short inclined lift that carries visitors from the Old Town up to the castle on the hill above. It was designed as part of the castle's renovation and opened on 28 December 2006. The idea is much older: in 1897 the then mayor, Ivan Hribar, wrote to the Austro-Hungarian authorities to ask for a lift up to the castle. The ride takes about a minute and is popular with tourists. As a photo subject it works best from the outside, because the lower station and the track climbing the wooded hillside make a clean, simple shape. Krekov trg, the square where the ride starts, is the only place where the funicular itself is the subject, and it is near the Central Market. You can photograph the line from the ground before or after a trip. Include a little of the square in the foreground to show where you are, and let the track lead the eye up the hill. Don't plan to shoot from inside the cabin, as the windows are dirty. If you want the castle hill with the whole Old Town beneath it, Čevljarski most (Cobbler's Bridge) gives a wider view across the Ljubljanica, though the funicular is only a small detail there, if you can see it at all.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Ljubljana, in the Old Town. The lower station is on Krekov trg, close to the Central Market, at the foot of the castle hill.
text.directions_text: There are no tram or railway stops listed for this spot, so head for Ljubljana's Old Town and the Central Market. Krekov trg is the square beside the market, and the lower funicular station is on its east side. From the Old Town itself it is a short stroll on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the station and the track together. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more of the square around the station. Use 2x or more to pick out the line climbing the hill.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Krekov trg (east side, by the lower funicular station (Krekov trg 4)). The funicular's lower station and the track climbing the wooded hill toward the castle, with the Old Town square in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up the track against one of them so it doesn't look tilted. Keep a strip of the square at the bottom of the frame and let the track lead up to the castle hill. For a different view, try Čevljarski most, where the funicular is only a small detail.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the station to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the bright sky doesn't wash out the hillside. Take a few frames, as people often walk through the square.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Daylight is best, when the wooded hillside and the station are clearly lit. Early in the day the square is likely to be quieter.

text.access_note: The funicular is a ticketed ride whose hours and fares vary, so check the official site before you go; photographing it from the square needs no ticket.

name: Nebotičnik
label: Nebotičnik
camera_source: No separate stand-here point: photographed at the spot itself (indoors, from its top, or right in front of it); drawn as the split pin.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/235168944: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Nebotičnik' (34 m across).
notes: Early skyscraper with a viewing terrace and café.

text.description:
Nebotičnik, which means 'the Skyscraper', is one of Ljubljana's most recognisable landmarks. It rises thirteen storeys to 70.35 m in the centre of the city. Architect Vladimir Šubic designed it in a mix of neoclassical and art-deco styles. It opened on 21 February 1933 and was then the tallest building in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. Some residents feared it would spoil the city's Baroque skyline of bell towers, so it was controversial when it went up.

It photographs well because the shape is so clear. A solid base leads to a plain tall shaft, and the top is crowned with a round colonnade and flagpole. Look for the four-metre sculpture of a woman on the side façade, level with the sixth floor. It makes a good detail shot.

To get the whole tower in one frame you need some distance, so step back from the building and look up. Close to the entrance you can only photograph the lower storeys and the stonework. The top floors hold a café, bar and observation deck, so you can also photograph the city from above. Remember that from up there you will not have the tower itself in the picture.
text.geographic_location: Nebotičnik stands in the centre of Ljubljana. A six-storey residential block by the same architect stands to its west.
text.directions_text: Head for the centre of Ljubljana and look up for the tall tower; it stands well above the buildings around it. The phone icon on the map is on the building itself, so once you arrive, walk a little way back to find a clear view of the full height. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the default lens (1x) for the whole tower from across the street. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you are close and want the full height. Use telephoto (2x-5x) for the colonnade at the top or the sculpture on the side façade.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. You cannot frame the tower from inside it, so walk back across the street until the whole height fits. For views over the city, go up to the observation deck instead.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line the sides of the tower up with the vertical lines so it does not lean. Keep the phone level, and tilt the camera up only a little. For a detail shot, zoom in on the female sculpture or the round colonnade on top.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the tower to focus. Then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky stays blue and the façade keeps its detail.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft daylight in the morning or late afternoon usually suits the stonework. After sunset, night mode can capture the tower against a darkening sky.

text.access_note: The tower's outside can be photographed from the street. The café, bar and observation deck are on the top floors, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: The tower is visible above surrounding buildings from many streets in the centre.
The whole tower only fits in a phone frame from some distance across the street.
Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually suits stone façades.
Night mode can work well on the tower against the sky after sunset.
From the observation deck, the tower itself is not in view.

name: Franciscan Church of the Annunciation
label: Franciscan Church
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Prešernov trg' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Prešernov trg' (relation/9375924): middle (117 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/176487479: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Franciscan Church of the Annunciation' (58 m across).

text.description: The Franciscan Church of the Annunciation is the pink Baroque church on Prešeren Square, in the middle of Ljubljana. It photographs well because the whole facade fits in one frame, with open granite paving in front and the stone entrance staircase leading the eye up to the doors. The pink is deliberate: the colour is symbolic of the Franciscan order, and it replaced an earlier white finish when the exterior was redesigned in 1858. The church itself was built between 1646 and 1660, with the bell towers following around 1720. Look up to the top of the facade for the copper statue of Our Lady of Loretto, and for the three niches with sculptures above the main portal. Since 2008 the church has been protected as a cultural monument of national significance. For the classic shot, stand at the southern end of the square and shoot north with the phone held upright, so the towers and pilasters stay straight. Go early in the morning if you can, when the square is quiet and the foreground is clear. Two alternatives are the footbridge by the Triple Bridge (labelled in English as the Fishmarket Footbridge), where the facade is reflected in the river, and Tromostovje, where the church sits behind the Prešeren statue with the bridge's lanterns in view.
text.geographic_location: The church stands on Prešeren Square in the centre of Ljubljana. The Franciscan monastery is right beside it, squeezed between Čop Street, Nazor Street and Miklošič Street.
text.directions_text: No tram or railway stops are listed for this spot, so head for Prešeren Square in the centre of Ljubljana. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in the full facade and the paving in front of it. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a calmer, less stretched look. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details such as the statue at the top and the niches above the portal.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Prešernov trg (Southern end of the square, shooting north toward the church with a wide-angle lens). The full pink Baroque facade of the church, with the square's granite paving in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and keep the phone upright and level, so the towers and pilasters don't lean. Leave a band of paving at the bottom of the frame to lead the eye up to the staircase and doors. If the square is busy, try the footbridge by the Triple Bridge (the Fishmarket Footbridge) for the reflection in the river, or Tromostovje for the church framed behind the Prešeren statue.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the pink facade to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the walls look washed out. Use a 2x-5x zoom rather than pinching in further when you photograph the statue and niches.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, before the market and café furniture fill the square.

text.access_note: The outside of the church is on an open public square, but it is a place of worship, so dress and behave respectfully; photography may not be allowed inside, so check the official site before you go.

name: Ljubljana Cathedral
label: Ljubljana Cathedral
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Zmajski most' (1 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Zmajski most' (way/867533647): middle (46 m across); moved 15 m off water.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/176486012: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Ljubljana Cathedral' (66 m across).
notes: Baroque cathedral with a green dome and bronze doors.

text.description:
Ljubljana Cathedral, officially the Church of Saint Nicholas, is easy to spot in the old town because of its green dome and twin towers. It stands on Ciril-Metodov trg, next to the Central Market and the Town Hall. A Gothic church once stood here, and the Baroque building that replaced it was put up between 1701 and 1706 and consecrated on 8 May 1707. The Jesuit architect Andrea Pozzo reworked the plan and added the dome. The two belfries are decorated with gilded apples, and the bronze doors date from 1996.

The building photographs well because the dome and towers make a clear skyline shape. The best-recommended view is from Zmajski most (the Dragon Bridge). From there you see the cathedral across the river, and one of the bridge's green dragon sculptures can sit in the foreground to give the picture depth. The square in front of the cathedral, Ciril-Metodov trg, is another option, where the cathedral forms the backdrop, but the market stalls can crowd the frame, particularly on weekdays. Kongresni trg is a separate square that offers a view with the mountains rising behind the cathedral.

The cathedral is some way off from the bridge, so a little zoom helps you fill the frame with the dome and towers. Take a few frames with and without the dragon, then choose the one that feels most balanced.
text.geographic_location: In the old town of Ljubljana, on Ciril-Metodov trg beside the Central Market and the Town Hall. Zmajski most, the recommended viewpoint, is a short walk away across the river.
text.directions_text: No tram or railway stop is listed for this spot, so start from the Central Market and Town Hall area. The cathedral is on Ciril-Metodov trg, right beside the market. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) so the dragon, the river and the cathedral all fit in. Because the cathedral is a little way off, try telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for a tighter shot of the dome and towers. Keep the ultra-wide (0.5x) for the square in front of the cathedral if you want the whole facade.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Zmajski most. The cathedral's green dome and towers seen across the river, with one of the green dragon sculptures of the bridge in the foreground. From here the cathedral lies to the south-west across the river.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put a dragon sculpture in one corner of the frame and let the dome and towers fill the space behind it. Turn on gridlines to keep the towers upright and the bridge edge level. Kongresni trg shows the cathedral with mountains rising behind it. From Ciril-Metodov trg, the square in front of the cathedral, the cathedral forms the backdrop, but the market stalls can crowd the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the dome to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky looks washed out. Try both 1x and a 2x-5x zoom, as the cathedral is some way from the bridge.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually suits the green dome. Go early if you want fewer people on the bridge. Weekdays are often the busiest for market stalls in front of the cathedral, so expect them to crowd that square then.

text.access_note: The cathedral is a working place of worship, so dress modestly if you go inside, and check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements; the bridge viewpoint is an open public place.

name: Town Square
label: Town Square
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Tromostovje' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Tromostovje' (relation/6583849): middle (54 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/5033210: the middle of the OpenStreetMap line 'Mestni trg' (196 m long).
notes: Historic old-town square beside the Town Hall.

text.description:
Town Square (Mestni trg) is one of Ljubljana's major squares, and it is the setting for Ljubljana Town Hall. In front of the Town Hall stands a copy of the Robba Fountain; the original is kept in the National Gallery. Opposite is the Krisper House, where Julija Primic, the inspiration of the poet France Prešeren, was born in 1816. The composer Gustav Mahler also lived there in 1881-82. Ljubljana Cathedral stands close by, at Cyril and Methodius Square.

The square photographs well from a little way off. From there you look across the river to the square and the old town rooflines, with the castle in the distance on a clear day. The river in the foreground gives the picture depth, and the buildings sit neatly in the frame.

Once you have the wide view, walk into Mestni trg itself for a closer picture of the fountain with the Town Hall facade behind it. The cobblestones are uneven, so watch your step while you line up the shot. Keep your phone steady against your body or the railing and take a few frames, as people often walk through the view.
text.geographic_location: Town Square is in Ljubljana's old town, in front of the Town Hall and a short walk from Ljubljana Cathedral.
text.directions_text: There are no Underground, train or tram stops at this spot, so start from Ljubljana's old town centre. Walk away from the river and the square opens up in front of you. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the full view across the river. Switch to the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the Town Hall and the rooflines, or the castle in the distance. Use ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of river and sky, as it makes the square look small.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Tromostovje (the embankment by the Triple Bridge on the Ljubljanica). A view across the river that takes in the Town Square and the old town rooflines, with the castle in the distance on a clear day.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the river along the lower third, with the rooflines across the middle. Zoom in a little if the castle is visible, so it does not shrink to a dot. For a closer alternative, walk into Mestni trg and shoot the Robba Fountain copy with the Town Hall facade behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the buildings to set focus, then slide the exposure down slightly if the sky is bright, so the facades keep their colour. Take a Live Photo if people are crossing the bridge, so you can pick the best frame afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunrise or sunset, for golden-hour light. The square is also worth a visit at other times of day.

text.access_note: The square and the embankment are open public space, but check the official site before you go if you plan to go inside any building.

name: Robba Fountain
label: Robba Fountain
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Tromostovje' (1 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Tromostovje' (relation/6583849): middle (54 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap node/313396512: the OpenStreetMap point 'Robba fountain'.
notes: Baroque fountain in front of the Town Hall.

text.description:
The Robba Fountain stands in front of Ljubljana Town Hall on Mestni trg (Town Square). Francesco Robba, an Italian sculptor, made the original in 1751. It is one of the city's most recognisable symbols. Three muscular figures, each with a dolphin and a water jug, sit at the foot of a 10-metre obelisk. They came to be read as the river gods of the Sava, Krka and Ljubljanica. The stepped base stands for the Carniolan mountains. The marble figures, the obelisk and the trefoil basin are all different stones, which gives the sculpture plenty of texture for a phone camera.

What you see in the square is a replica, put in place in 2006. The restored original has been in the National Gallery of Slovenia since 2008, so the photo shows the copy.

The best view for a phone is from the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje). From there the fountain is framed across the river, with Ljubljana Castle in the background, and it is a calmer spot than the square. If you want the classic postcard shot, walk into Mestni trg and put the fountain in the foreground with St Nicholas Cathedral rising behind it.
text.geographic_location: The fountain is in Ljubljana's old town, on Mestni trg (Town Square), directly in front of the Town Hall. The Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica is a short walk away.
text.directions_text: Head for the old town and Town Hall on Mestni trg. From there the fountain lies to the south-east, about 2 minutes on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) on the bridge to include the river, the fountain and the castle. Switch to telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the three figures and the obelisk across the water. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you move into the square and want the Town Hall and the cathedral in the same frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Tromostovje (the Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica, looking back toward the square). A framed view of the fountain across the river, with Ljubljana Castle visible in the background.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the fountain on one of the lower thirds, with the river in the foreground and the castle higher up on the other side. Keep the phone level so the obelisk stays upright. For the classic alternative, stand in Mestni trg with the fountain in the foreground and St Nicholas Cathedral rising behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the white marble figures to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the stone keeps its detail. Take a few shots in a row, as people often walk through the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Right after sunrise is recommended, as it brings the best light on the sculptures and fewer tour groups. The best light can vary, so check on the day and try both morning and late afternoon if you can.

text.access_note: The fountain stands in an outdoor public square and the bridge is a public crossing, but check the official site before you go for any events or works.

name: Butchers' Bridge
label: Butchers' Bridge
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Mesarski most' (3 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/867534136: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Butcher Bridge' (42 m across).
notes: Pedestrian bridge with sculptures and love padlocks.

text.description: Butchers' Bridge is a short, wide footbridge over the Ljubljanica that links the Central Market with the embankment on the opposite bank. It works almost like a small square on the water, so there is plenty to look at without leaving the deck. The bronze sculptures by Jakov Brdar are the main draw: Adam and Eve, a startled Satyr and Prometheus, plus smaller frogs and shellfish along the top of the fence. Steel-wire railings carry the padlocks that couples began adding soon after the bridge opened on 10 July 2010. The bridge was designed by Jurij Kobe and measures about 33 metres long and 17.3 metres wide. It stands on a spot where Jože Plečnik had imagined a much grander, covered bridge in the 1930s, which was never built. For a phone, this is a close-up place. Fill the frame with one sculpture or a cluster of padlocks, and let the river and the market colonnade fall softly behind. Stand at the phone icon on the map and you are right on the deck. Take a wider shot along the bridge to show the glass edges and the railings leading the eye. Keep an eye on the glass walkway, which can be slippery when wet, and mind other visitors who stop to look at the sculptures.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Ljubljana, spanning the Ljubljanica between the Central Market and Petkovškovo nabrežje (the Petkovšek Embankment).
text.directions_text: There is no station or tram stop right at this spot, so start from the Central Market and walk to the river; the bridge crosses the Ljubljanica right there and can be reached on foot. The phone icon on the map is on the bridge itself, so there is no further walk once you reach the deck. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the sculptures and padlocks. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) for a shot along the whole deck, and use 2x if your phone has it to isolate a single figure.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Stand on the deck, at the bronze sculptures and the padlocked railings.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Pick one sculpture or a row of padlocks as your subject and let the river and colonnade blur behind it. Turn on gridlines and place the figure on a third. For a second shot, step back and use ultra-wide to show the railings leading along the bridge.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bronze to set focus, then use the exposure slider to bring the brightness down a little so the metal keeps its detail. Portrait mode can add a soft background to a sculpture, but check the edges of the figure afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon or around sunset, when low light falls on the bronze and the glass.

text.access_note: The bridge is a public footbridge, open to walk across at any time; still, check the official site before you go in case of works or winter coverings on the glass.

name: Križanke
label: Križanke
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Križevniška soteska' (2 web pages); placed at the stretch of Križevniška soteska nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/179744955: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Križanke outdoor theatre' (65 m across).
notes: Former monastery turned open-air theatre, redesigned by Plečnik.

text.description:
Križanke is a former monastery in the middle of Ljubljana that now works as an open-air theatre and festival space. Building is believed to have started in 1228, when it was a monastery of the Teutonic Knights. The church was rebuilt in Baroque style in 1714-15 to a Greek-cross plan by the Venetian architect Domenico Rossi. The monastery was nationalised in 1945. In the early 1950s the city asked Jože Plečnik to turn the empty buildings into a festival venue, and his work was finished in 1956.

The usual photo is inside the arcaded courtyard, but a quieter outside angle is Križevniška soteska, a narrow stone-walled passage along the outer walls of the complex. It leads out towards Zoisova cesta. The tall walls make a natural frame, and the passage gives your picture a clear sense of depth and leads the eye along the length of the old monastery. Confirm the exact spot on site.

If you have time, also look at Križevniška ulica, where the church spire rises behind the street. Inside the complex, the courtyard has stone portals and, in the Hell Courtyard, a ceiling of small lights. The area can be closed during events and concerts, so check the schedule before you go. Keep your phone level so the walls stay straight, and allow a few minutes to try both a wide shot and a closer one.
text.geographic_location: Križanke stands in the old centre of Ljubljana, on French Revolution Square (Trg francoske revolucije).
text.directions_text: From the centre of Ljubljana, head for French Revolution Square (Trg francoske revolucije), or go by taxi or hired scooter if the distance is too far to walk. From there the theatre outline lies to the west, about 1 minute on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit both walls and the passage in one frame. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural, less stretched view of the stonework. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out details such as stone texture or the far end of the passage.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Križevniška soteska (the passage on the former monastery grounds, shot looking toward Zoisova cesta). A narrow stone-walled gorge along the outer walls of Križanke, framing the complex with the passage leading out to Zoisova cesta. Confirm the exact spot on site, then frame the shot so the walls of Križanke frame the picture from the outside. The theatre outline itself lies to the west of where you stand.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up a vertical grid line with a wall edge so the walls do not lean. Put the passage opening towards Zoisova cesta in the centre or on a third. Keep the walls on both sides for a framed look. For a different view, Križevniška ulica has the church spire behind a street of summer flowers, and the arcaded courtyard inside the complex is another option.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the brightest part of the passage to set focus, then lower the exposure slider a little so the sky or the bright end does not wash out. Hold the phone steady with both hands, as the passage can be dim. Take a few frames to be safe.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft daylight suits the stone walls best, such as morning or late afternoon, when the passage is less likely to have harsh contrast. Check the event schedule first, as the area can be closed for concerts.

text.access_note: The complex is a venue used for events and concerts and can be closed at those times, so check the official site before you go.

name: Ljubljana Opera House
label: Opera House
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Opera' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Opera' (node/4569038859): point.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/179746610: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'SNG Opera in balet Ljubljana' (95 m across).

text.description:
The Ljubljana Opera House is the national opera building of Slovenia and the home of the national opera and ballet company. It was first called the Provincial Theatre and was built between 1890 and 1892 by the Czech architects Jan Vladimír Hráský and Anton Hruby, in the Neo-Renaissance style. Until the German Theatre opened in 1911, it staged productions in both Slovene and German. After that it used only Slovene.

It photographs well because the front is so clear and orderly. Ionic columns carry a pediment with a tympanum over the entrance, and two niches at the sides hold the allegorical statues of Tragedy and Comedy by the sculptor Alojz Gangl. Standing in front of the main facade on the Župančičeva street side, you can fit the whole columned front into one picture. You can then step closer for detail shots of the sculptures.

The building sits between the Slovenian Parliament on one side and the National Museum and National Gallery on the other. These make useful landmarks if you are looking for it.

For a phone, start with a straight-on shot of the full front, then take a second, tighter frame of the tympanum or one of the statues. Dusk is a good time to come, because the portico is lit then. Interior photos are usually limited and depend on the venue's rules, so ask staff if you go to a performance.
text.geographic_location: The Opera House stands at Župančičeva 1 in central Ljubljana. It is between the Slovenian Parliament building and the National Museum and National Gallery.
text.directions_text: No Underground, rail or tram stop is listed for this spot. Start from the central Ljubljana area near the Parliament building, the National Museum or the National Gallery, which are the neighbouring landmarks on either side of the Opera House. The address is Župančičeva 1. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you are close, so the whole columned front fits in. Use the default lens (1x) for a more natural look from a little further back. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for the tympanum sculptures and the Tragedy and Comedy statues.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (in front of the main facade, Župančičeva 1 (Župančičeva street side)). The full Neo-Renaissance front of the building with its columned entrance, the tympanum sculptures above it, and the niches holding the Tragedy and Comedy statues.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and line the columns up with the vertical lines so the building does not lean. Keep the entrance in the centre for a balanced shot. Then take a tighter frame of the sculptures at the top or in the niches.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the facade to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright so the stonework keeps its detail. At dusk, let night mode work and hold the phone steady against something solid.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Dusk, when the portico is lit. Check the lighting on the day.

text.access_note: The facade can be photographed from the street, but check the official site before you go if you want to see or photograph inside, as that depends on venue rules.

name: Tivoli Castle
label: Tivoli Castle
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Jakopičevo sprehajališče' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Jakopičevo sprehajališče' (relation/15342459): middle (249 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/5803213: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Tivolski grad' (40 m across).
notes: Mansion in Tivoli Park housing the graphic arts centre.

text.description:
Tivoli Castle is really a mansion, set in Tivoli Park at the foot of Rožnik Hill. This is the building to photograph, not Ljubljana Castle on the hill in the Old Town. It photographs well because the Jakopič Promenade, the park's long main avenue, ends right at its front. Trees line both sides and lead the eye to the building, so the picture is naturally symmetrical. The promenade also hosts outdoor photo exhibitions, which can add interest in the foreground, though they change from time to time.

The current building dates from the 17th century and stands on the ruins of an earlier Renaissance castle. It began as a Jesuit property and later became the bishop's summer residence. In 1852 Emperor Francis Joseph I gave it to Marshal Joseph Radetzky, who renovated it in the Neoclassical style, which gives it the look it has today. Since 1967 it has housed the International Centre of Graphic Arts.

For your own photo, stand at the lower end of the promenade and look uphill along the avenue. Keep the mansion in the middle of the frame and let the trees form the sides. If you walk closer, look for the four cast iron dogs in front of the building, made in 1864 by Anton Dominik Fernkorn. They make a fun foreground detail. Mornings are quieter, so you are more likely to get the avenue without crowds.
text.geographic_location: In Tivoli Park, in the Rožnik District, northwest of Ljubljana city centre and at the foot of Rožnik Hill. The mansion stands at the top end of the Jakopič Promenade, the continuation of Cankar Street.
text.directions_text: No Underground, rail or tram stop is listed for this spot. Head for Tivoli Park, northwest of the city centre, and follow Cankar Street and the Jakopič Promenade. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to capture the whole avenue and the mansion at its end. Try the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for a tighter view of the building with the trees close around it.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Jakopičevo sprehajališče (Lower end of the promenade, looking uphill along its axis toward the mansion). The mansion filling the end of a long, tree-lined avenue, a symmetrical view that leads the eye to the building. The mansion fills the far end of the long, tree-lined walk, so you get a symmetrical view with the building straight ahead, to the west.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Centre yourself on the middle of the avenue and turn on gridlines so the trees stay level and the mansion sits on the centre line. If an outdoor photo exhibition is on, use the ultra-wide (0.5x) to bring a panel into the foreground. For a different view, Tivoli Park shows the mansion on its hill with the Ljubljana skyline and Nebotičnik below.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the mansion to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the facade keeps its detail. Keep the phone upright and use the gridlines to avoid sloping verticals.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Mornings are described as quieter and moodier, so they are the best bet for a clear view down the avenue. Afternoons are busier.

text.access_note: The park and promenade are open public space, but the gallery inside the mansion may be ticketed, so check the official site before you go.

name: Ljubljana Town Hall
label: Town Hall
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Mestni trg' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Mestni trg' (way/5033210): point nearest the subject (195 m long).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/615385067: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Mestna občina Ljubljana' (71 m across).

text.description: Ljubljana Town Hall, known locally as the Rotovž, is the seat of the City Municipality of Ljubljana and sits on Mestni trg (Town Square) in the city centre, close to the Cathedral. It photographs well because the front is a tidy Baroque façade with a clock tower, and a Robba fountain stands right in front of it, so you get architecture and a bit of street life in one frame. The first building here was Gothic, dated 1484. Between 1717 and 1719 it was renovated in a Baroque style with Venetian inspiration, which gave it the gable front, the loggia and the three-part staircase you see today. The fountain outside is a replica of Francesco Robba's work; the original, finished in 1751, is kept in the National Gallery. From the middle of the square you can line up the north façade with the fountain in front and, behind it, the Cathedral and the castle hill. The square is compact, so it is hard to shoot wide, and your phone's ultra-wide lens will help. If you have a minute, look at the alternative view in the arcaded courtyard (Mestna hiša), where arches frame a fountain and niches. This is a working municipal building, so events or weddings can sometimes block the front view. Take a few frames with and without people in front of the fountain, then choose later.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Ljubljana, on Mestni trg (Town Square), close to the Cathedral. The Robba fountain stands directly outside the building.
text.directions_text: Head for Mestni trg in the city centre, close to Ljubljana Cathedral. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to get the whole façade, clock tower and fountain into one frame in this tight square. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural look with less stretching at the edges. If your phone has telephoto (2x-5x), use it for the clock tower or the fountain details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Mestni trg (centre of the square, facing the town hall's north façade). The Baroque façade and clock tower of the town hall, with the Robba fountain in front and the Cathedral and castle hill in the background.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn the phone upright (portrait) so the clock tower fits, and switch on gridlines to keep the building's vertical lines straight. Put the fountain in the lower part of the frame and the façade above it. Keep the phone level, as tilting it back makes the building lean. For a second view, try the arcaded courtyard (Mestna hiša), where the arches frame a fountain and niches.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the façade to set focus and exposure, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the building keeps its detail. If people walk through, a Live Photo lets you pick a moment with a clear foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, when the sun rises behind the castle. The square is largely in shade in the afternoons.

text.access_note: Mestni trg is an open public square, but the town hall is a working municipal building, so check the official site before you go if you want to see inside, as photography rules may differ for exhibitions and ceremonial rooms.
claims_not_in_sources: Tilting a phone upwards makes tall buildings appear to lean backwards.
The ultra-wide lens can stretch objects near the edges of the frame.
Gridlines help keep vertical lines straight.

name: Prešeren Monument
label: Prešeren Monument
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Tromostovje' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Tromostovje' (relation/6583849): middle (54 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/1223766264: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Prešern Memorial' (13 m across).
notes: Statue of the national poet France Prešeren.

text.description: The Prešeren Monument is a bronze statue of France Prešeren, the Slovene national poet, and one of the best-known monuments in Slovenia. The poet stands in formal dress, with a vest and unbuttoned coat, holding a book that stands for his Poems. Above him a muse sits on a rock with a laurel branch. The poet's figure is 3.5 metres high and the whole monument is 9.6 metres. It was unveiled on 10 September 1905, and more than 20,000 people were there. The statue is about 70 m from the Triple Bridge, on the square just to the north, and the classic photo is taken from the bridge. From there the bronze poet fills the foreground and the pink Franciscan Church rises behind him, with the river Ljubljanica in the frame. The pink church gives a soft colour backdrop and makes the dark bronze stand out. It looks especially good at sunset or in golden-hour light. The square also has other angles. A closer, more intimate view puts the statue in front of the church. Another fills the frame with the church facade and keeps the monument visible below. Look at the pedestal too, which has two bronze reliefs showing scenes from Prešeren's poems. Midday and event days can be busy, and so can 8 February, Prešeren Day. If you want a clear view of the statue, go early or later in the day.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Ljubljana, on the eastern side of Prešeren Square, in front of the Central Pharmacy Building. The square is next to the Ljubljanica river and the Triple Bridge.
text.directions_text: Head for Prešeren Square in the centre of Ljubljana, then walk to the square-side end of the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje). The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the classic view of the statue with the church behind it. Switch to 2x or the telephoto if your phone has one, to bring the church closer and pick out the poet and the muse. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only in the square itself, when you want the whole monument and the facades in one frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Tromostovje (square-side end of the Triple Bridge). The bronze poet in the foreground with the pink Franciscan Church behind him, framed across the Ljubljanica. The statue is to the north of you.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the statue on one of the vertical lines, so the church fills the space beside it. Keep the horizon level, and keep the muse and the poet's head clear of the church roofline if you can. For a closer alternative, walk into Prešernov trg and shoot the statue from the square, with the Franciscan Church rising behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bronze figure to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the pink church and the sky do not wash out. If people walk through the frame, take a Live Photo or a short burst and pick the cleanest frame afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunset or golden hour. Midday and event days are busier, so go early or later in the day if you want fewer people in the frame.

text.access_note: The monument stands in a pedestrianised public square and photography is unrestricted there, but drones are restricted over the historic centre, so check the official site before you go if you plan to fly one.
claims_not_in_sources: Midday and event days are usually busier, so early or later visits give clearer views of the statue.
The pink colour of the church makes the dark bronze statue stand out in photos.
Drones are restricted over Ljubljana's historic centre.

name: Cobblers' Bridge
label: Cobblers' Bridge
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Ribja brv' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Ribja brv' (way/883439865): middle (26 m across); moved 15 m off water.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/883439866: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Cobblers' Bridge' (31 m across).

text.description: The Cobblers' Bridge (Čevljarski most) is a pedestrian bridge over the Ljubljanica river, linking two of the main parts of medieval Ljubljana. It photographs well because it is more than a crossing. Corinthian pillars trace the shape of the bridge, and Ionic pillars carry the lamps. Behind it you get the colourful riverside houses and the castle on the hill. The current stone bridge was designed by Jože Plečnik in 1931 and became part of his UNESCO World Heritage listing in 2021. There has been a bridge here since at least the 13th century. It began as a wooden bridge with butchers' stalls, until the smell led the Emperor of the day to pay for them to be moved. Shoemakers took over the booths, which is how the bridge got its name. From there you look back towards the Cobblers' Bridge with the houses and the castle in one picture. It is also worth walking onto the Cobblers' Bridge itself. The colonnaded balustrade makes a good foreground, with the river and the Old Town facades on both banks. Expect people, especially during the Sunday flea market and when buskers play in the evening.
text.geographic_location: The bridge is in the Old Town of Ljubljana, crossing the Ljubljanica river between the two historic riverbanks, with the castle hill rising behind it.
text.directions_text: No tram or train stop is listed for this spot, so head for the Old Town in central Ljubljana. From there the Cobblers' Bridge is about 3 minutes on foot to the south, along the river. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to fit the bridge, the riverside houses and the castle in one frame. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if the footbridge is busy and you cannot step back. Use 2x or 3x telephoto to pick out the castle or the lamp pillars.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Ribja brv. A view from the neighbouring footbridge back toward the Cobblers' Bridge, with the colourful riverside houses and the castle visible in one frame. If you want the castle view from the Cobblers' Bridge itself, the middle of the bridge is the most common choice, and the southern end is another option.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and put the bridge on the lower third, with the castle hill above it. If you are on the Cobblers' Bridge itself, use the colonnaded balustrade as a foreground line that leads the eye along the river. Keep the phone level so the river banks do not slope.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the bright sky or the castle to set focus and exposure, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky keeps its colour. In the evening, night mode can help, but hold the phone against the railing so the picture stays sharp.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Avoid Sunday flea-market hours and evenings with buskers if you want fewer people on the bridge.

text.access_note: The bridge is pedestrian-only and open to the public.

name: Ljubljana Central Market
label: Central Market
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Vodnikov trg' (1 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Vodnikov trg' (relation/17326269): middle (189 m across).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q12034073: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Open-air market and Plečnik colonnade along the river.

text.description:
Ljubljana Central Market is a working food market on the right bank of the Ljubljanica River, and it is one of the liveliest places in the city to take photos. The long, curved market hall was designed by Jože Plečnik in the 1930s and built in the early 1940s. It runs between the Triple Bridge and the Dragon Bridge. Large semi-circular windows face the river, and a colonnade lines the street side. Two open-columned loggias break up the building so the river stays in view. Since August 2021 the market has been part of Plečnik's legacy on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

The square in front, Vodnikov trg, has been an outdoor market since the 1895 earthquake cleared the buildings that stood there. Today you will find stalls of produce, flowers and cheese, with the arcades and the riverside halls behind them. That mix of colourful close-up detail and handsome architecture is why it works so well on a phone. Start at the stalls, then step back to take in the long line of the hall.

For a wider view of the building, try the Dragon Bridge (Zmajski most) or the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje). From there the hall stretches along the water. Arrive early if you can, because the square is quietest before the tour groups come.
text.geographic_location: In central Ljubljana, on the right bank of the Ljubljanica River, on and around Vodnikov trg (Vodnik Square). The market hall stretches between the Triple Bridge and the Dragon Bridge.
text.directions_text: No Underground, rail or tram stop is listed for this spot, so head for the Triple Bridge area in the centre of Ljubljana and walk from there. Walk along the right bank of the river towards the Dragon Bridge and you will reach Vodnikov trg, in front of the market arcades. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the stalls and the street scene. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) when you want the whole arcade, and to the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for close shots of produce, flowers and cheese without crowding the stallholders.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Vodnikov trg (open-air market area on the square beside the arcades). Stalls of produce, flowers and cheese seen at close range, with the Plečnik halls running along the riverside behind them. The main market hall is to the north.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put a colourful stall in the foreground and let the arcade or hall fill the background. Turn on the gridlines and keep the long lines of the colonnade level. For the full length of the hall, walk to the Dragon Bridge (Zmajski most), where the building can be mirrored in the water, or to the Triple Bridge (Tromostovje), where the bridge railings frame the view.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the stall or face you want sharp, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so bright flowers and fruit keep their colour. Portrait mode suits close shots of produce, but check that the edges look natural. Live Photos can catch a moment of market activity.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Before 10 am, when it is quieter and the tour groups have not yet arrived.

text.access_note: The square and the market stalls are open to the public, and the market trades daily except Sundays, but check the official site for current days and times before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Mirroring of the hall in the river is easiest to see from the Dragon Bridge.
Close-up shots of stallholders are generally better after a friendly nod or a word with the seller.
The market is in the central part of Ljubljana, within walking distance of the old town.
Portrait mode can sometimes produce odd edges around irregular shapes such as flowers.
